Definition: % of production databases with automated failover and redundancy (e.g., AlwaysOn, RAC, Mirroring).
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: HA exists for critical DBs only
Level 2 - Developing: HA exists for critical DBs only. Manual failover required.
Level 3 - Defined: HA standardized for all production DBs. Failover is automated but rarely tested.
Level 4 - Managed: Multi-node/site HA with 99.9% availability. Regular failover drills performed.
Level 5 - Optimized: 99.99%+ availability. Active-Active setups. Zero-downtime maintenance and automated healing.
Notes and Evidence: Implement HA/DR strategy using Oracle RAC, Data Guard, or cloud-native HA capabilities to reduce single-point-of-failure risk.

Definition: % of successful backups and validated restores within defined RPO/RTO.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No formal backups. Success unknown. Recovery never tested.
Level 2 - Developing: Backups run but not monitored. Success rate <85%.
Level 3 - Defined: Backups monitored centrally. 85-95% success. Annual recovery testing.
Level 4 - Managed: >98% success. Failures trigger auto-alerts. Quarterly recovery validation.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% success. Automated, continuous recovery testing. Immutable backups.
Notes and Evidence: Backup operations are automated through scheduled scripts/tool, and recovery procedures are periodically validated during refresh activities. However, recovery execution remains manual and centralized reporting/validation can be improved.

Definition: Adherence to security baselines (e.g., CIS Benchmarks) and encryption status.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No hardening. Default passwords in use. No encryption.
Level 2 - Developing: Manual hardening applied. Some encryption at rest.
Level 3 - Defined: Standardized hardening policy. Automated scanning. Data-at-rest encryption for all.
Level 4 - Managed: 90%+ compliance with CIS. TDE and Data-in-Transit encryption enforced.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% compliance. Real-time drift detection. Automated masking and tokenization.
Notes and Evidence: Basic security controls are implemented; however, encryption standards, password governance, and centralized compliance enforcement require improvement.

Definition: Management of DBA and Application account access, including MFA and least privilege.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Shared sa or root passwords. No MFA. Broad access for all.
Level 2 - Developing: Named accounts for DBAs. MFA on management plane. Periodic manual review.
Level 3 - Defined: RBAC enforced. MFA for all privileged access. Quarterly access audits.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated JIT (Just-in-Time) access. 95%+ MFA coverage. Integrated with PAM vault.
Level 5 - Optimized: Zero-trust model. No permanent privileged accounts. AI-based anomaly detection for DB access.
Notes and Evidence: Privileged access is managed through standard database authentication without MFA or enterprise PAM integration.

Definition: Process for scanning, identifying, and remediating DB-specific CVEs and configuration flaws.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No scanning. Vulnerabilities only addressed during major upgrades or after a breach.
Level 2 - Developing: Periodic manual scans. No formal SLA for patching critical vulnerabilities.
Level 3 - Defined: Monthly automated vulnerability scans. Critical patches applied within 30 days.
Level 4 - Managed: Real-time vulnerability assessment. Integrated with SOC/SIEM. 95% of DBs meet patch SLAs.
Level 5 - Optimized: Continuous zero-day protection. Automated virtual patching and instant remediation of drift.
Notes and Evidence: Vulnerability remediation activities are partially aligned with quarterly patching cycles; however, centralized vulnerability scanning and SLA-driven remediation require improvement.

Definition: Monitoring of slow queries, index fragmentation, and execution plans.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No monitoring. Performance issues handled reactively based on user complaints.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic resource monitoring (CPU/Memory). Occasional manual tuning.
Level 3 - Defined: APM/DB monitoring tools in place. Slow query logs reviewed weekly.
Level 4 - Managed: Proactive tuning based on wait-state analysis. Automated alerts for performance degradation.
Level 5 - Optimized: AI-driven query optimization. Predictive performance analytics. Zero manual tuning required.
Notes and Evidence: Oracle OEM-based monitoring provides proactive visibility into database performance, query bottlenecks, and resource utilization, enabling operational performance management.

Definition: % of DBs on supported versions and current security patch levels.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No patching schedule. Many EOL versions in production.
Level 2 - Developing: Inconsistent patching. Vulnerability remediation takes >60 days.
Level 4 - Managed: Automated patch deployment. 95%+ compliance within 30 days of release.
Level 5 - Optimized: Zero EOL versions. Self-patching/Green-Blue deployment pipelines. Real-time compliance.
Notes and Evidence: Quarterly patch management processes are established and operationally maintained; however, further automation and compliance reporting opportunities exist.

Definition: % of DB deployments handled via IaC (Terraform, Ansible) or Self-Service Portals.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Manual DB creation. Configuration varies every time.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic scripts for installation. 50% manual effort remains.
Level 3 - Defined: Standardized images/templates. DB-as-a-Service (DBaaS) available for Dev.
Level 4 - Managed: 90%+ IaC coverage. Automated configuration management and drift detection.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% automated lifecycle. GitOps workflow. Self-healing configuration.
Notes and Evidence: Provisioning activities are primarily manual, supported by scheduled backend scripts without Infrastructure-as-Code or orchestration framework integration.

Definition: Transition from legacy VM-based DBs to Cloud-Native/PaaS (RDS, Cloud SQL, Aurora) or NoSQL.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Entirely on-prem legacy VMs. No cloud strategy.
Level 2 - Developing: Some Lift & Shift to cloud VMs (IaaS). No PaaS usage.
Level 3 - Defined: Strategy defined for PaaS adoption. 30% of non-prod on PaaS/DBaaS.
Level 4 - Managed: 70%+ of workloads on PaaS. Significant use of NoSQL/NewSQL where applicable.
Level 5 - Optimized: 100% Cloud-Native or Serverless where possible. Multi-region/Global distribution.
Notes and Evidence: Cloud migration initiatives are in progress; however, migration activities remain largely manual without standardized cloud-native operational practices.

Definition: Integration of database schema changes into the application deployment pipeline.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Manual SQL scripts run by DBAs. No version control for schemas.
Level 2 - Developing: SQL scripts stored in Git, but deployments are still manual.
Level 3 - Defined: Automated schema migrations (e.g., Liquibase/Flyway) in non-prod environments.
Level 4 - Managed: Full CI/CD for DB changes in all environments. Automated rollback capability.
Level 5 - Optimized: DataOps fully realized. Self-service schema changes with automated policy guardrails.
Notes and Evidence: Database deployment and change management activities are currently executed manually without CI/CD pipeline integration.

Definition: Reduction of sprawl by consolidating small DBs onto shared platforms or multi-tenant clusters.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: Massive sprawl; hundreds of underutilized standalone instances. High licensing waste.
Level 2 - Developing: Initial inventory completed. Manual consolidation of dev/test environments.
Level 3 - Defined: Multi-tenancy (e.g., SQL Instances/Oracle CDB) used for 40% of workloads.
Level 4 - Managed: 80% consolidation achieved. Standardized T-shirt sizing for all DB deployments.
Level 5 - Optimized: Extreme density. Serverless/Elastic scaling used to eliminate idle resources. Zero ghost DBs.
Notes and Evidence: Database environments are primarily deployed as standalone instances without consolidation or high-density architecture optimization.

Definition: The ability of the system to detect and fix common DB issues without human intervention.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: 100% manual intervention for every alert or disk-full event.
Level 2 - Developing: Basic scripts for log truncation or service restarts.
Level 3 - Defined: Automation library for common tasks (e.g., automated index rebuilds, disk expansion).
Level 4 - Managed: Event-driven automation. 70% of routine alerts resolved by automated workflows.
Level 5 - Optimized: Fully autonomous. Self-healing DB clusters that scale, patch, and tune without DBA input.
Notes and Evidence: Operational incidents and service interruptions currently require manual intervention and remediation activities.

Definition: Use of Machine Learning to predict failures, optimize performance, and manage security.
Level 1 - Ad Hoc: No AI usage. Monitoring is purely threshold-based (e.g., alert at 90% CPU).
Level 2 - Developing: Basic trend analysis. Using vendor-provided Advisors for query tuning.
Level 3 - Defined: Centralized AIOps platform ingesting DB logs for anomaly detection.
Level 4 - Managed: Predictive alerting (alerts trigger before failure). AI-driven capacity planning.
Level 5 - Optimized: Generative AI integrated for SQL generation/optimization. Autonomous DBA bots manage ops.
Notes and Evidence: AI/ML-driven operational analytics and predictive monitoring capabilities are currently not implemented.
